author: reek
body: The platform seam. Lens ships to two substrates from one source: Target N runs this chapter's bodies natively, Target B replaces them at C# emission with runtime-preamble bindings. Every function declared here is one seam point: a real Codex definition that the csharp plug's Platform Seam Overrides table intercepts by name (CSharpEmitterExpressions.codex), rewriting call sites to the emitted preamble class and skipping the native body entirely. Code that cites this chapter is target-independent by construction - the same call is a Codex DB executor dispatch on Target N and a SqlClient round trip on Target B.

author: reek
body: lens-sql-exec executes one SQL statement and returns the result rows, each row a list of column values rendered as text. On Target B the binding is _LensSql.exec: connection string from the LENS_SQL_CONN environment variable, rows streamed one at a time off a SqlDataReader. The native body below is an honest stub returning the empty row list; the real native handler arrives with the Lens service wiring (DESIGN Phase 6), where the statement routes into the apps/data RelAlgebra executor instead of a barbarian warehouse.

author: reek
body: The signature is deliberately pure for this first proof. An effect-typed form, lens-sql-exec : Text -> [LensSql] List (List Text), is the destination: it makes database access visible in every caller's row and lets capability manifests bound what a dashboard may touch. That requires declaring the LensSql effect and threading handlers through the native call graph, which is Phase 3 seam work - recorded here so the follow-up is not rediscovered.

author: reek
body: The [LensHttp] seam is two calls shaped for a one-request-at-a-time service loop. lens-http-next blocks until the next HTTP request arrives on the given port and answers with exactly three texts: the method, the request path, and the whole request body, in that order. The body arrives with carriage returns already stripped: CCE has no carriage return, so the Target B binding normalizes barbarian line ends at the seam boundary and a caller splits on newline alone. An empty list means the platform has no listener, which is what the native stub below answers today: a native caller's serve loop sees the empty list and shuts down cleanly instead of spinning. The real native handler arrives with the codex.os.net service wiring, the same Phase 6 seam work recorded for lens-sql-exec above.
